declared.title: Motivating Personal Growth by Seeking Discomfort
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 13); Crossref search « Woolley Fishbach motivating personal growth by seeking discomfort » (2026-11-26)

population: 5 experiments with 2,163 adults: improvisation classes, expressive writing, news on COVID-19, opposing political views, gun violence

findings.text: Told to seek discomfort as a sign of growth, people engaged more in personal-growth activities and felt they reached their goal more than with standard instructions, measured in the same session

support.sentence: Across these areas of personal development, seeking discomfort as a signal of self-growth motivated engagement and increased perceived goal achievement relative to standard instructions.

findings.text: The effect appeared only in areas of personal growth that cause immediate discomfort

support.sentence: Consistent with our theorizing, results showed that these effects occurred only in areas of personal growth that cause immediate discomfort.

limits: one laboratory (as woolley-2016-fun and woolley-2025-resolutions); no independent replication found (counter-evidence search, 2026-11-23)
goal achievement is perceived (self-reported), not observed; no follow-up: everything is measured in the same session (OSF protocols and preregistrations)
experiment 1 (improvisation classes) assigned by half-class, not individually, and not preregistered; experiments 2 to 5 preregistered, online
experiment 2 (expressive writing) preregistered its persistence measures (words, seconds) with the prediction « no effect »; full text closed
an instruction to seek discomfort, against standard instructions (« write », « learn », « develop skills »): not the choice of a long-term struggle
countries not given in the abstract; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
